tasks.notes: Stale header comment in `fleet/retire.mjs` (lines 31–36, unchanged by this patch). The module docblock still says the integration branch name "is still read once per run, as the `head=` filter of the closed-PR list". After this change a terminal pair's integration branch name is read twice — the new `state=open` read in `openPullOf` (patch lines 114–122) and `pullsToPatch`'s `state=closed` read — so the sentence is now false. The rest of the docblock was updated for the status read (the new paragraph at lines 40–51 and the `--dry-run` paragraph at 61–64), which makes this one paragraph the only stale line left. Nothing in the exam or the docs-pin suite catches it, and the fix is inside this task's own FILES.; Small duplication: `openPullOf` (patch lines 114–122) repeats `pullsToPatch`'s owner derivation (`String(target).split('/')[0]`) and `pulls?state=…&head=<owner>:<integration branch>` path construction, differing only in the `state=` value and in returning the first row rather than patch candidates. A shared `pullsOf(exec, target, run, state)` returning the row array, with `pullsToPatch` filtering it, would spell the head filter once. The added doc comment already flags that `state=open` is the only difference, so this is advisory only — the behaviour is exactly what M4 asks for and is pinned by legs (h)/(i).; Code quality (rule 5, copy-pasted logic): `openPullOf` in `fleet/retire.mjs` reproduces `pullsToPatch` line-for-line for the parts that matter — `const owner = String(target).split('/')[0]` and the `repos/${target}/pulls?state=<s>&head=${owner}:${integrationBranchFor(run)}` path — differing only in the literal `state=open` vs `state=closed` and in what it does with the rows. The comment on `openPullOf` even says so ("`state=open` is the only difference from the closed read below"). A single reader, e.g. `async function pullsHead (exec, target, run, state) { const owner = String(target).split('/')[0]; const payload = await ghRead(exec, `repos/${target}/pulls?state=${state}&head=${owner}:${integrationBranchFor(run)}`); return Array.isArray(payload) ? payload : [] }` with `openPullOf` returning `rows[0] ?? null` and `pullsToPatch` filtering it, would keep the two reads from drifting apart (the exam pins both call strings, so the refactor is safe). Behaviour is correct as written; this is advisory only.; Toolchain coupling in the exam: the new `#706 (l)/M7` block in `fleet/tests/test_retire.mjs` ends with `spawnSync('python3', ['-m','pytest','tests/test_docs_agree_with_code.py','-q','-p','no:cacheprovider'], { cwd: REPO_ROOT })` and asserts `status === 0`. That is the same command the Proof already carries as its third `Run:` (driver evidence: exit 0), so `node fleet/tests/test_retire.mjs` now fails on any machine without python3/pytest for a reason that has nothing to do with the sweep. The two in-file assertions above it — that the contract's `**The two tags**` bullet and the runbook's `## Rollback` section each carry the literal `— skipped`, and that neither document shows a `?ref=ultra/evidence-run-` — are the part of leg (l) worth keeping inside the node exam; the pytest spawn could be dropped and left to the `Run:` that already owns it. No requirement is left unverified either way, so this blocks nothing.; Explicit error path (rule 5): `openPullOf` returns `rows[0]` unconditionally and the caller builds `` `PR #${open.number} open` ``, so a pulls row without a numeric `number` would print `run <N>: live (PR #undefined open) — skipped` and land that string in `live[].why`. `pullsToPatch` directly above already guards this shape (`if (typeof number !== 'number') continue`). Selecting the first row whose `number` is a number — or falling back to a why of `open PR` — would match the neighbouring code's care. The exam's fixtures always carry `number`, and M4 only specifies the well-formed case, so this changes nothing that is graded.; concern: fleet/tests/test_retire.mjs is the Proof's Test: path (peer-owned), but the task's Files names it and its BASE version would have failed the TEST COMMAND once the status read existed (every pair would read as 'no status page'). I updated only the pins the task's Context names as moving — the makeSeam contents rule + a per-run PAGES map, the open/closed split in the /pulls? rule, sweepOf's filter, the (e) closed-PR pin, leg (g)'s dry-run call sequence, and loggingShims' gh dispatch/count — plus one process leg for the gated case. I wrote no new assertion legs for the peer's (a)-(l); expect the driver's overlay to replace this file wholesale.; concern: M4 formats the skip line from the first open-PR row's `number` verbatim (`PR #${row.number} open`); a non-empty array whose first row has no numeric `number` would render `PR #undefined open`. The Machine text specifies only 'the first row's number', so no guard was added.
